glosses: To break or separate into pieces.

examples.text: Break up the cheese and put it in the salad.

examples.text: It broke up when it hit the ground.

glosses: To upset greatly; to cause great emotional disturbance or unhappiness in.

examples.text: "I remember his wail at the meeting, which began: 'In fifty years experience of scientific intercourse----' It quite broke the old man up."

glosses: To end a (usually romantic or sexual) relationship.

examples.text: She broke up with her boyfriend last week.

glosses: To end a (usually romantic or sexual) relationship with each other.

examples.text: Jane and Stephen broke up.

glosses: To dissolve; to part.

examples.text: The meeting finally broke up after a three-hour discussion.

Accordingly, as ſoon as the hurry was over, and the ſervants, as ſhe thought, all gone to ſleep, ſhe ſtole out of her bed, and went down ſtairs, naked to her ſhift as ſhe was, with a deſign to ſteal them […]

glosses: Of a school, to close for the holidays at the end of term.

glosses: Of a conversation, to cease to be understandable because of a bad connection; of a signal, to deteriorate.

glosses: To stop a fight; to separate people who are fighting.

examples.text: The police came in to break up the disturbance.

glosses: To become disorganised.

examples.text: England's superior conditioning began to show in the final quarter and as the game began to break up, their three-quarters began to stamp their authority on the game. glosses: To cut or take to pieces for scrap.

To divide (a thing) into separate parts.

examples.text: Separate the articles from the headings.

Butterfly taxonomists, however, like the triple-barrelled name approach and dote on subspecies. As a result, the numbers of ant species and butterfly species are not directly comparable.

The mesosphere may be described as the earth's intermediate or middle atmosphere, which separates the thermosphere above from the ozonosphere (or stratosphere) below, both of which are responsible for absorption of most of the ultraviolet part of the solar radiation and preventing it from reaching the earth's surface.

glosses: To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect.

examples.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?

glosses: To cause (things or people) to be separate.

examples.text: If the kids get too noisy, separate them for a few minutes.

glosses: To divide itself into separate pieces or substances.

examples.text: The sauce will separate if you don't keep stirring.

glosses: To set apart; to select from among others, as for a special use or service.

examples.text: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.

glosses: Apart from (the rest); not connected to or attached to (anything else).

examples.text: This chair can be disassembled into five separate pieces.

glosses: Not together (with); not united (to).

examples.text: I try to keep my personal life separate from work.
